title: A Growing Universe, and Is Anyone Out There?

pages.text: On a warm night, a child lies on a mat outside, looks up, and asks how much is out there. It is one of the oldest questions people have asked. The universe is everything that exists: all of space and time, and all the matter and energy in them. Evidence from many kinds of observation shows that it is about 13.8 billion years old. It began in an extremely hot, dense state and has been expanding and cooling ever since. Scientists call that beginning the Big Bang. The name is a little misleading. It was not an explosion at one place in space. Space itself began to stretch, everywhere at once. Over time, gravity pulled gas together to form the first stars and galaxies.

Evidence from many kinds of observation shows that it is about 13.8 billion years old.
It began in an extremely hot, dense state and has been expanding and cooling ever since.
Scientists call that beginning the Big Bang.
The name is a little misleading.
It was not an explosion at one place in space.
Space itself began to stretch, everywhere at once.
Over time, gravity pulled gas together to form the first stars and galaxies.
pages.alt: A timeline band running from a bright glowing start on the left, through the first stars and galaxies, to the present-day sky on the right.

pages.text: In the 1920s, astronomers measured the light from distant galaxies and made a discovery. Almost all of them are moving away from us, and the farther away a galaxy is, the faster it moves. Think of raisins in bread dough. As the dough rises, every raisin moves away from every other raisin. No raisin is the centre. In the same way, the space between groups of galaxies is stretching. Galaxies inside one group are held together by gravity and do not drift apart. In 1998, astronomers found that the expansion of the universe is speeding up. The unknown cause is called dark energy.

No raisin is the centre.
In the same way, the space between groups of galaxies is stretching.
Galaxies inside one group are held together by gravity and do not drift apart.
In 1998, astronomers found that the expansion of the universe is speeding up.
The unknown cause is called dark energy.
pages.alt: A loaf of rising dough with raisins moving apart, beside a matching sketch of groups of galaxies moving apart as space stretches.

pages.text: To see farther, we build better telescopes. The Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, orbits above Earth’s blurring air. Astronomers once pointed it at a patch of sky that looked empty, far smaller than the full Moon, and collected light for more than eleven days. The picture showed about 10,000 galaxies. The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in December 2021, has a mirror 6.5 metres wide. It sees infrared light, which has a longer wavelength than the light our eyes detect. It has found galaxies whose light set out less than 300 million years after the Big Bang. That light has travelled for more than 13 billion years.

pages.text: A planet that orbits a star other than the Sun is called an exoplanet. The first one orbiting a Sun-like star was found in 1995. By September 2025, NASA’s list of confirmed exoplanets had passed 6,000, with thousands more waiting to be checked. Astronomers find most of them by watching a star dim slightly when a planet passes in front of it. Some exoplanets orbit in the habitable zone of their star. That is the range of distances where a planet could be warm enough, but not too hot, for liquid water. Liquid water is essential for life as we know it.

pages.text: So far, the honest answer is that we do not know. No life has been confirmed anywhere beyond Earth. But the search is serious science. Researchers look for biosignatures: chemicals or patterns that living things could produce. In 2025, scientists reported that a rock drilled on Mars by NASA’s Perseverance rover contains minerals that might have been made by ancient microbes. Ordinary chemistry might also explain them. Only laboratory tests on Earth could decide. This is how science works. An exciting claim is not accepted until the evidence is strong and other explanations have been ruled out.

pages.text: Ghana is part of this search for knowledge. At Kuntunse, near Accra, stands a dish 32 metres wide. It was built to carry telephone and television signals by satellite. Ghanaian and South African engineers converted it into a radio telescope, and the Ghana Radio Astronomy Observatory opened in 2017. It studies radio waves from space and can link with telescopes in other countries to act as one giant instrument. In the same year, GhanaSat-1, a small satellite built at All Nations University in Koforidua, was released into orbit. The next discoveries will need new scientists and engineers. Some of them may be reading this.

activities.question: What does it mean to say that the universe is expanding?
options: The space between groups of galaxies is stretching, so they move apart

activities.question: Why is looking at a very distant galaxy like looking back in time?
options: Its light took billions of years to reach us
Distant galaxies are younger than Earth

activities.question: What is the habitable zone of a star?
options: The hottest region, closest to the star
The range of distances where a planet could have liquid water

activities.question: Apply it: A headline says, "Gas that may be a sign of life found on a distant planet." What is the most scientific response?
options: Accept that alien life has been found
Treat it as a possibility and wait for more evidence
Ignore it, because life elsewhere is impossible

items: The Big Bang, about 13.8 billion years ago

glossary.definition: Everything that exists: all space, time, matter, and energy.

Dark energy: the unknown cause of the speeding-up of the universe’s expansion.
